claim_checks.claim: It removed the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions
claim_checks.page_says: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport. ... Make MCP stateless: remove the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake.
claim_checks.note: Both removals are listed in the 2026-07-28 changelog.

claim_checks.claim: A request missing a required key is rejected with `-32602`, and with HTTP 400 on HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: The required fields are the _meta keys listed just above the passage; MUST on the page, plain statement in the doc.

claim_checks.claim: On HTTP there is nothing to shut down: each request is its own POST
claim_checks.page_says: Each request is its own POST ... servers could assign a session via the Mcp-Session-Id header (terminated with HTTP DELETE) ... None of these mechanisms are part of this revision.
claim_checks.note: The page removes sessions and their DELETE termination (GET/DELETE answered 405), so the 2026-07-28 HTTP binding has no termination step.

claim_checks.claim: Legacy (2025-11-25) step 5: `notifications/tools/list_changed`, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection
claim_checks.page_says: listChanged: Support for list change notifications (for prompts, resources, and tools) ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: Name gap for the legacy era. The cell sits in the Legacy (2025-11-25) column, so only the 2025-11-25 pages cited as [4] (lifecycle, transports) count; they say tool list-change notifications exist and that a GET SSE stream may carry notifications, but never give the method name. [13] names notifications/tools/list_changed only for the 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen stream (another version). The name does appear in the 2025-11-25 security page, which the doc labels [4a-sess], not [4], and does not cite here.

claim_checks.claim: A missing resource is error `-32602` in 2026-07-28 (it was `-32002` before; clients should still accept `-32002`)
claim_checks.page_says: If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (Invalid Params). ... clients SHOULD also accept -32002 as a resource not found error
claim_checks.note: Changelog [3] confirms the change from -32002 to -32602 (SEP-2164).

claim_checks.claim: The client gathers the input and retries the original request with a new `id`, `inputResponses` and the echoed `requestState`
claim_checks.page_says: Client gathers the requested information from the user or other sources, then retries the original request including the additional requested information. ... The JSON-RPC id MUST be different
claim_checks.note: The page also says the client MUST echo back the exact requestState when one was returned; the doc's preceding sentence marks requestState as optional, so the echo is conditional in context.

claim_checks.claim: Worked example (2026-07-28, from the spec): `tools/call` id 2 returns an `input_required` result asking for a GitHub username via form elicitation; the client retries `tools/call` as id 3 with `inputResponses: {"github_login":{"action":"accept","content":{"name":"octocat"}}}` and the same `requestState`
claim_checks.note: The tools page example shows id 2 with resultType input_required, a form-mode elicitation for the GitHub username, and the id 3 retry carrying the same requestState.

claim_checks.claim: Sessions, 2025-11-25: optional `MCP-Session-Id`; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client `DELETE` to end
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request. ... SHOULD send an HTTP DELETE
claim_checks.note: Optional session and 404 after termination (MUST) are supported. '400 without it' states a SHOULD rule as plain fact and drops its conditions (servers that require a session id; requests other than initialization). 'client DELETE to end' states a SHOULD as plain fact, and the page lets the server answer 405 to it.

claim_checks.claim: Existing HTTP+SSE server: keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP (why: deprecated)
claim_checks.page_says: Servers wanting to support older clients should: Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint”
claim_checks.note: Advice in a decision table, matching the page's 'should'; the same section says existing implementations SHOULD migrate to Streamable HTTP and that HTTP+SSE is deprecated.

claim_checks.claim: Need server push of tool-list changes: `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) or GET stream (legacy)
claim_checks.page_says: toolsListChanged | boolean | Receive notifications/tools/list_changed when tools change ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: [15] covers the 2026-07-28 option. For the legacy option, [4] transports lets a client open a GET SSE stream on which the server may send notifications, and [4] lifecycle lists tool list-change notifications. The cell names no method, so the S4 name gap does not apply here.

claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: Leaves out the qualifier 'security': the page requires security best practices, and the claim widens that to best practice in general. The modal (MUST) matches.

claim_checks.claim: Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. ... insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: HTTP 403 Forbidden status code
claim_checks.note: Raises a SHOULD to MUST. The leading 'Server must' (and the flow's 'steps are normative unless marked') covers every clause, including the 403 insufficient_scope response, but the page has SHOULD for that response and for listing the needed scopes. Token validation, audience check and 401 are MUST on the page and are supported.

claim_checks.claim: Resources: servers must validate URIs and sanitize `file://` paths against traversal
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate all resource URIs ... Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving file:// resources
claim_checks.note: The claim text ends at the mark after 'Resources'; judged on the full line it introduces.

claim_checks.claim: Related attacks with required mitigations: ... SSRF through metadata URLs (clients should require HTTPS and block private ranges, and use an egress proxy on servers)
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients SHOULD require HTTPS for all OAuth-related URLs in production environments ... operators SHOULD consider using an egress proxy that enforces network policies
claim_checks.note: Leaves out the condition 'in production environments' on the HTTPS rule, and writes 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' as 'should use' (raised short of MUST level). Blocking private ranges matches its SHOULD. The clause's own 'should' governs over the sentence's 'required mitigations' lead-in, and the page does make clients deployed to a server 'MUST consider SSRF risks and implement appropriate mitigations'.

violations.evidence: S4: in the 1.6 table, the Legacy (2025-11-25) column names `notifications/tools/list_changed`, but the 2025-11-25 pages cited as [4] never give that name, and [13] is a 2026-07-28 page.
S12: flow step 9 puts the 403 insufficient_scope response under 'Server must'; [26] says 'the server SHOULD respond with: HTTP 403 Forbidden'.

S8: Sessions row, 2025-11-25 cell. '400 without it' and 'client DELETE to end' are SHOULD rules in [4] written as plain fact, and the 400 rule's condition (servers that require a session id, requests other than initialization) is left out.
S11: 3.5 Scope leaves out 'security' from [26]'s 'MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol'.
S14: in 4.4 the SSRF clause leaves out 'in production environments' from the HTTPS rule and turns [30]'s 'SHOULD consider using an egress proxy' into 'should use'.

Found in the conflict audit, outside the fixed sample, so not counted in factual_grounding. In 3.2, 'No feature has been removed yet ✅[21]' leaves out [21]'s qualifier: 'No features have been removed under this policy yet.' Without it, the line contradicts the doc's own 2.2 and the changelog [3] ('Remove ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed').

Diataxis. No heading does the role 2 job: concept architecture is mixed with mechanism in 1.1 and 2.1. Role 1 exists only inside the Summary. The role 4 heading (section 6) lists the experiments but holds none of their inputs or outputs; the real runs sit inline in 1.4, 1.5 and 3.1. The free-form deep-dive layout has no research-heading set (sections_present false).

patch_instructions.action: In the 1.6 table, step 5, Legacy column: either cite the 2025-11-25 page that names the method ("... server sent events as a consequence of a tool call such as a notifications/tools/list_changed", the doc's [4a-sess]) as `✅[4][4a-sess]`, or reword it to 'tool list-change notification (`listChanged` capability), sent on a GET SSE stream (HTTP) or the open stdio connection ✅[4]' and keep the method name only in the 2026-07-28 column ✅[14].

Split 3.5 flow step 9 in two: 'Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired tokens must get `401` ✅[26]. For insufficient scope the server should respond `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and should list the scopes the operation needs in `scope` ✅[26].'

3.1 table, Sessions row, 2025-11-25 cell: 'optional `MCP-Session-Id`; servers that require one should answer 400 to requests without it (other than initialize); must answer 404 after ending the session; clients should `DELETE` to end it, and the server may answer 405 ✅[4]'.
3.5 Scope: 'Implementations using alternative transports must follow established security best practices for their protocol ✅[26]'.

4.4 Related attacks: change the lead-in to 'Related attacks and their mitigations:' and the SSRF clause to 'SSRF through metadata URLs (clients deployed to a server must consider SSRF risks; clients should require HTTPS for OAuth-related URLs in production and should block private and reserved IP ranges; operators of server-side clients should consider an egress proxy) ✅[30]'.

3.2: 'No feature has been removed under the deprecation policy yet ✅[21]', and add that the 2026-07-28 changelog removed `ping`, `logging/setLevel` and `notifications/roots/list_changed` outside that policy ✅[3].

Structure: give role 2 a section of its own (move the 1.1 roles and the 2.1 primitive table there, with no mechanism text). Turn section 6 into the worked-examples section holding the E1/E4/E5/E6 wire transcripts with their inputs and outputs, or relabel it as verification status and move the transcripts into a dedicated worked-examples section.
